subject: Career
title: Fidgeting and Nervous Tells
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fidgeting and Nervous Tells.

hook.text: You don't notice you're bouncing your leg. The interviewer does. Nervous tells leak constantly.

buildup.text: Common tells: touching face, clicking pens, shifting in chair, avoiding eye contact under pressure.

discovery.text: These signals activate the interviewer's threat detection. Anxiety becomes contagious.

twist.text: Eliminating tells isn't about suppression. It's about having a calm anchor — hands resting, feet flat.

climax.text: Practice interviews on camera expose tells you'd never catch otherwise.

punchline.text: Calm body, calm mind. The interviewer feels it too.

quiz.question: Why are nervous tells problematic in interviews?
options: Anxiety becomes contagious and triggers threat detection

details.summary: Fidgeting behaviors like tapping, hair touching, and leg bouncing are unconscious stress signals that interviewers interpret as anxiety, dishonesty, or lack of preparation. Awareness is the first step to managing these tells.
details.whyItMatters: Nervous tells can undermine an otherwise strong interview performance because nonverbal signals carry more weight than verbal content in ambiguous situations.
takeaways: Record mock interviews to identify your personal nervous tells
Anchor your hands on the table or armrests to reduce fidgeting
Channel nervous energy into purposeful hand gestures

faq.question: What are the most common nervous tells interviewers notice?
faq.answer: Touching the face or hair, bouncing a knee, clicking a pen, avoiding eye contact, and speaking too quickly are the top five. Most people have one or two dominant tells that intensify under stress. Identifying yours through video review is essential.

faq.question: How do you manage interview anxiety without suppressing all body movement?
faq.answer: Practice box breathing before the interview and use deliberate hand gestures during answers to channel energy productively. Complete stillness looks as unnatural as constant fidgeting. Aim for composed, purposeful movement.
